page_title: Timing Automatic Mac Time Tracker – Manual Timers Optional

sources.entry: Timing - Automatic time tracking with productivity insights and billing-friendly records.

summary.name: Timing
summary.one_liner: Timing is a native macOS time tracker that automatically records which apps, websites and documents you use, so you can review and bill your time without manual timers.
use_cases: Automatically logging billable hours for freelancers
Reviewing where time went across apps and websites
Creating accurate client timesheets and invoices
Tracking time spent on calls, meetings and calendar events
Filing tracked activities into projects with rules
summary.what_it_does: Timing runs on the Mac and automatically logs the apps, websites, documents, chat apps and calendar events you use, detecting when you stop using the Mac so idle time can be excluded. AI summaries and automatic grouping suggest time entries and show key patterns. Users create rules (by ⌥-dragging) to permanently assign activities to projects, and can drag and drop to assign time in a timeline. Data can be exported as PDF, XLSX, CSV or HTML for timesheets and invoices, and time can be imported from Screen Time and viewed in a web app, with optional cloud sync.
notable: Automatic tracking of apps, websites and documents with no start/stop timers
Imports mobile app usage from Screen Time and supports MCP for AI agents like Claude Code and Codex
Native macOS app with local storage; private/incognito tabs discarded and exclusion list available
Exports to PDF, XLSX, CSV, HTML and has a GrandTotal invoicing plug-in
caveats: Free trial is 30 days; the page does not state ongoing free-tier limits or full paid pricing
Cloud sync is opt-in; tracked data otherwise stays local on the Mac
Team admins see only aggregate times for team projects
